steps.q: A country's factories, shops and offices each produce goods and services. If you added up the value of everything produced across the whole country in a year, what would you have?
steps.right: The value of everything the economy produces
steps.wrong: The value of everything the government spends
steps.hint: Think about adding up output from every firm in the country, not just government spending.

steps.q: Prices rise by 10% this year but firms produce exactly the same quantity of goods as last year. Has the country actually produced more, even though the measured value in pounds is higher?
steps.right: No, the same amount was produced
steps.hint: The extra pounds come from higher prices, not from more goods leaving the factories.
